frq.skill: Limit definition of the derivative and tangent lines
frq.context: Let f be the function defined by f(x) = x³ − 4x + 2 for all real numbers x.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Evaluate lim(x→2) [f(x) − f(2)]/(x − 2). Show the computations that lead to your answer.
parts.solution: f(2) = 8 − 8 + 2 = 2, so the limit is lim(x→2) (x³ − 4x)/(x − 2) = lim(x→2) x(x − 2)(x + 2)/(x − 2) = lim(x→2) x(x + 2) = 2(4) = 8. (Equivalently, this limit is by definition f′(2).)
rubric: 1 pt: recognizes the limit as f′(2) or correctly factors and cancels (x − 2) in the difference quotient
1 pt: value 8

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Using the limit definition of the derivative, f′(x) = lim(h→0) [f(x + h) − f(x)]/h, show that f′(x) = 3x² − 4.
parts.solution: f(x + h) − f(x) = (x + h)³ − 4(x + h) + 2 − (x³ − 4x + 2) = 3x²h + 3xh² + h³ − 4h. Dividing by h (h ≠ 0) gives 3x² + 3xh + h² − 4. As h → 0, the terms 3xh and h² approach 0, so f′(x) = lim(h→0) (3x² + 3xh + h² − 4) = 3x² − 4.
rubric: 1 pt: correct difference quotient [f(x + h) − f(x)]/h with f(x + h) expanded
1 pt: algebra: cancels the h from every remaining term
1 pt: evaluates the limit as h → 0 to obtain 3x² − 4 (limit notation used correctly throughout)

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Write an equation of the line tangent to the graph of f at the point where x = 2.
parts.solution: The point of tangency is (2, f(2)) = (2, 2), and the slope is f′(2) = 3(4) − 4 = 8, consistent with part (a). An equation of the tangent line is y = 2 + 8(x − 2), or equivalently y = 8x − 14.
rubric: 1 pt: uses the point (2, 2) (computes f(2) = 2)
1 pt: tangent line equation with slope f′(2) = 8, e.g. y = 2 + 8(x − 2)

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Find all values of x at which the line tangent to the graph of f is horizontal. Justify your answer.
parts.solution: A tangent line is horizontal where f′(x) = 0. Setting 3x² − 4 = 0 gives x² = 4/3, so x = −2√3/3 and x = 2√3/3 (equivalently x = ±2/√3). These are the only solutions of f′(x) = 0, so they are exactly the x-values where the tangent line is horizontal, because a horizontal tangent occurs precisely where the derivative equals 0.
rubric: 1 pt: sets f′(x) = 0 (i.e., 3x² − 4 = 0)
1 pt: both values x = ±2√3/3 with justification that horizontal tangents occur exactly where f′(x) = 0

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: On what open intervals contained in −4 < x < 4 is f increasing? Give a reason for your answer.
parts.solution: f is increasing on (−4, −2) and on (2, 4) because f′(x) > 0 on those intervals. From the graph, f′ is positive for −4 < x < −2 and for 2 < x < 4, and negative for −2 < x < 2.
rubric: 1 pt: identifies both intervals (−4, −2) and (2, 4)
1 pt: reason: f is increasing because f′(x) > 0 on those intervals

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the x-coordinate of each point at which f has a local maximum or a local minimum on −4 < x < 4. Justify your answers.
parts.solution: f has a local maximum at x = −2 because f′ changes sign from positive to negative there. f has a local minimum at x = 2 because f′ changes sign from negative to positive there.
rubric: 1 pt: local maximum at x = −2 with justification (f′ changes from positive to negative)
1 pt: local minimum at x = 2 with justification (f′ changes from negative to positive)

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: On what open interval is the graph of f concave down? Find the x-coordinate of each point of inflection of the graph of f. Justify your answers.
parts.solution: The graph of f is concave down on (−4, 0) because f′ is decreasing on that interval (the segments of the graph of f′ have negative slopes −2 and −1 there). The graph of f is concave up on (0, 4) because f′ is increasing there. There is a point of inflection at x = 0 because f′ changes from decreasing to increasing at x = 0.
rubric: 1 pt: concave down on (−4, 0)
1 pt: point of inflection at x = 0 only
1 pt: justification: f′ is decreasing on (−4, 0) and changes from decreasing to increasing at x = 0

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Write an equation of the line tangent to the graph of f at x = 1.
parts.solution: From the graph, f′(1) = −1 (on the segment from (0, −2) to (2, 0), which has slope 1, the value at x = 1 is −1). Since f(1) = 5, the tangent line is y = 5 − (x − 1), that is, y = −x + 6.
rubric: 1 pt: f′(1) = −1 read from the graph
1 pt: tangent line equation y − 5 = −1(x − 1) (or equivalent)

frq.context: At a water treatment plant, a storage tank contains 150 gallons of water at time t = 0. During the time interval 0 ≤ t ≤ 10 hours, water is pumped into the tank at the rate E(t) = 8 + 6 cos(t/3) gallons per hour, and water drains out of the tank at the rate L(t) = 10e^(−0.05t) gallons per hour. Let W(t) be the amount of water, in gallons, in the tank at time t.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: How many gallons of water are pumped into the tank during the time interval 0 ≤ t ≤ 10 hours?
parts.solution: The amount pumped in is the accumulation of the in-rate: ∫ from 0 to 10 of E(t) dt = ∫ from 0 to 10 of (8 + 6 cos(t/3)) dt = 80 + 18 sin(10/3) ≈ 76.570 gallons.
rubric: 1 pt: sets up the definite integral ∫ from 0 to 10 of E(t) dt
1 pt: answer 76.570 gallons (accept 76.569 to 76.570)

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Is the amount of water in the tank increasing or decreasing at time t = 4 hours? Give a reason for your answer.
parts.solution: W′(t) = E(t) − L(t). At t = 4, E(4) = 8 + 6 cos(4/3) ≈ 9.411 gallons per hour and L(4) = 10e^(−0.2) ≈ 8.187 gallons per hour, so W′(4) = E(4) − L(4) ≈ 1.224 > 0. Because W′(4) > 0 (water is entering faster than it is draining), the amount of water in the tank is increasing at t = 4.
rubric: 1 pt: considers W′(4) = E(4) − L(4) (or compares E(4) and L(4) numerically)
1 pt: concludes increasing with reason W′(4) ≈ 1.224 > 0, i.e., E(4) > L(4)

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find W(10), the amount of water in the tank at time t = 10 hours.
rubric: 1 pt: expression W(10) = 150 + ∫ from 0 to 10 of (E(t) − L(t)) dt (initial condition plus net accumulation)
1 pt: answer 147.876 gallons (accept 147.875 to 147.876)

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: For 0 ≤ t ≤ 10, find the time t at which the amount of water in the tank is an absolute maximum. Justify your answer.
parts.solution: W′(t) = E(t) − L(t) = 0 when 8 + 6 cos(t/3) = 10e^(−0.05t); solving with a calculator gives t ≈ 4.774. This is the only critical point of W on (0, 10): W′(t) > 0 for 0 ≤ t < 4.774 and W′(t) < 0 for 4.774 < t ≤ 10, so W increases before t ≈ 4.774 and decreases after. Therefore the amount of water is an absolute maximum at t ≈ 4.774 hours.
rubric: 1 pt: sets W′(t) = 0, i.e., E(t) = L(t)
1 pt: justification that W′ changes sign from positive to negative at the only critical point (or a candidates test comparing W(0), W(4.774), W(10))

frq.context: Let R be the region in the xy-plane enclosed by the graphs of f(x) = 4 − x² and g(x) = x + 2, as shown in the figure. The graphs intersect at the points (−2, 0) and (1, 3).

parts.label: a
rubric: 1 pt: limits of integration x = −2 to x = 1 (from the intersection points)
1 pt: integrand (4 − x²) − (x + 2), top curve minus bottom curve
1 pt: antiderivative and answer 9/2

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the volume of the solid generated when R is revolved about the horizontal line y = −1.
parts.solution: Both curves lie above y = −1 on [−2, 1]. Outer radius: (4 − x²) − (−1) = 5 − x²; inner radius: (x + 2) − (−1) = x + 3. Volume = π ∫ from −2 to 1 of [(5 − x²)² − (x + 3)²] dx = π ∫ from −2 to 1 of (x⁴ − 11x² − 6x + 16) dx = π[x⁵/5 − 11x³/3 − 3x² + 16x] from −2 to 1 = π(143/15 + 316/15) = 153π/5.
rubric: 1 pt: form π ∫ [(outer radius)² − (inner radius)²] dx with limits −2 to 1
1 pt: correct radii 5 − x² and x + 3 (each shifted by +1 for the axis y = −1)
1 pt: answer 153π/5

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: The region R is the base of a solid. For this solid, each cross-section perpendicular to the x-axis is a rectangle whose height is 3 times its width in the base. Find the volume of the solid.
parts.solution: For each x in [−2, 1], the width of the rectangle is w(x) = (4 − x²) − (x + 2) = 2 − x − x², and its height is 3w(x), so the cross-sectional area is A(x) = 3(2 − x − x²)². Volume = ∫ from −2 to 1 of 3(2 − x − x²)² dx = 3 ∫ from −2 to 1 of (x⁴ + 2x³ − 3x² − 4x + 4) dx = 3(81/10) = 243/10.
rubric: 1 pt: cross-sectional area A(x) = 3[(4 − x²) − (x + 2)]²
1 pt: volume integral ∫ from −2 to 1 of A(x) dx (correct limits, no π)
1 pt: answer 243/10

frq.context: A particle moves along the x-axis so that its velocity at time t, for 0 ≤ t ≤ 5, is given by v(t) = t² − 6t + 8. The position of the particle at time t is x(t), and x(0) = 3.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the acceleration of the particle at time t = 1. Is the speed of the particle increasing or decreasing at t = 1? Give a reason for your answer.
parts.solution: a(t) = v′(t) = 2t − 6, so a(1) = −4. Since v(1) = 1 − 6 + 8 = 3 > 0 and a(1) = −4 < 0, the velocity and acceleration have opposite signs at t = 1, so the speed of the particle is decreasing at t = 1.
rubric: 1 pt: states speed is decreasing WITH reason: v(1) = 3 > 0 and a(1) = −4 < 0 have opposite signs

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find all times t, 0 ≤ t ≤ 5, at which the particle changes direction. Justify your answer.
parts.solution: v(t) = t² − 6t + 8 = (t − 2)(t − 4) = 0 at t = 2 and t = 4. Since v(t) > 0 on (0, 2), v(t) < 0 on (2, 4), and v(t) > 0 on (4, 5), the velocity changes sign at both t = 2 and t = 4. Therefore the particle changes direction at t = 2 and t = 4.
rubric: 1 pt: identifies t = 2 and t = 4 (sets v(t) = 0 and solves)
1 pt: justification that v(t) changes sign at each of t = 2 and t = 4 (positive to negative at t = 2, negative to positive at t = 4)

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the position of the particle at time t = 3.
parts.solution: x(3) = x(0) + ∫₀³ v(t) dt = 3 + [t³/3 − 3t² + 8t] from 0 to 3 = 3 + (9 − 27 + 24) = 3 + 6 = 9. The particle is at x = 9 at time t = 3.
rubric: 1 pt: expresses position as x(3) = x(0) + ∫₀³ v(t) dt (or an equivalent antiderivative with the initial condition x(0) = 3)

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Find the total distance traveled by the particle over the time interval 0 ≤ t ≤ 5.
parts.solution: Total distance = ∫₀⁵ |v(t)| dt. Splitting at the sign changes t = 2 and t = 4 with F(t) = t³/3 − 3t² + 8t: ∫₀² v dt = 20/3, ∫₂⁴ v dt = 16/3 − 20/3 = −4/3, and ∫₄⁵ v dt = 20/3 − 16/3 = 4/3. Total distance = 20/3 + |−4/3| + 4/3 = 28/3. The particle travels 28/3 units.
rubric: 1 pt: sets up total distance as ∫₀⁵ |v(t)| dt or splits the integral at t = 2 and t = 4
1 pt: correct antidifferentiation and evaluation of the three pieces (20/3, −4/3, 4/3)
1 pt: total distance = 28/3
